title: About the Tools in Data Science category
content:
This category is created to address subject-specific queries related to Tools in Data Science

- Why should people use this category? What is it for?

The larger goal of the Discourse forum is to act as a Knowledge base for the course. You can make this more productive by

  • Elaborating your question sufficiently and supporting it with steps that you have already tried at your end before posting this question

  • Sharing additional content or explanations related to the topic being discussed

    -  Are there any rules for posting in this category?

  • Before you create a new post, review the existing threads to see if there are already highly similar or identical postings. Discourse will suggest similar posts once you start typing titles

  • Tag the post appropriately so that it gets indexed correctly in our Knowledge Base. For instance, if your query is on an Activity Question in Week 1 then use the tags #activity-question, #week-1

  • Provide a meaningful title to your post that contains the topic/details of your query so that it can be searched by others easily. For instance: Do not use the titles like “AQ1.1 Q3” which just gives question number alone. Instead use a more meaningful title like - “Need help in calculating the N^{th} prime number”

  • Type in your question and explanations rather than pasting images or screenshots.

    - What is NOT Permitted in this category?

  • Being argumentative or sarcastic

  • Use of abusive/strong language

  • Posting support/logistics related query

  • Unnecessarily tagging Faculty/Instructors in posts

  • Posting Solutions or discussing solutions to graded assignments

    - Who will be moderating the content in this forum?

The foum will be moderated by Course Instructors. They will have the authority to decide whether a post violates forum rules/guidelines. You can flag/report any such violations that you observe by clicking on icon on the post. Please do mention the reason why you are flagging the topic.

  - What are the disciplinary actions if some one violates the rules and guidelines of the forum?

The flagged posts that violates forum rules/guidelines will be hidden. Repeated violation of the rules can result in the offender being removal from the forum.

title: Are paid AI models necessary to do well in ROE?
content:

For example, the layered encoding challenge is impossible to solve for the free version of ChatGPT. I asked the same question to Claude (free tier). So, considering that the ROE is worth 20% of the course grade, and some of the highest weightage questions of the ROE are solvable only with paid AI tools, do I need to buy ChatGPT Plus/Claude Pro plans to get an A/S in this course? title: Validation Bug Q6 GA0
content:
I was doing Q6 of GA0. And the validation script was also reading the colours along with the const colours; basically, it was checking the whole code for every single colour and comparing them. Is a part of GA0 to learn to ‘cheat’ the validation script also? Because in more than 1 question, we have had to not only answer them but also arrange the code in an absurdly specific way so the script understands how to pass it.

image947×868 80.7 KB

Think about it this way: the chart’s visual output is determined by every color in the file. If your CSS has background: #ff0000 and your palette has #ffffff → #000000, the file as a whole is not a clean sequential encoding , there’s a rogue red sitting in there. The script has no way to know which colors are “intentional palette” vs “accidental interference,” so it checks everything.
The question is asking you to submit a focused, minimal chart… not a full themed webpage. Strip it back to just what the chart needs to exist and render correctly.

23f1002856:

Is a part of GA0 to learn to ‘cheat’ the validation script also?

Yes it’s by purpose like that.

This behavior appears to be intentional, not a validation bug.

For this question, keep the submitted HTML/CSS/JS minimal and include only the colors required for the chart. The validator checks the file as a whole, so extra colors in CSS, styling, backgrounds, or unrelated page decoration can be treated as part of the submitted visual output. Remove any unnecessary styling and keep only what is needed for the chart to render correctly.

TDS May 26 Announcements General
Your distortion description has to match the source code exactly. The javascript function looks like this: function X(t, o, e) { if (t === "A") { let n = o.toFixed(1); return [`inflates tiny deltas by ${n}x`, `magnifies small movement about ${n}x`, `makes mild change look ${n}x`] } return t === "B" ? ["rescaled axis fakes synchronized trend", "dual-axis scaling manufactures false correlation", "secondary scale distorts cross-series comparison", `right axis stretched …

For more simplification, i made a console script to extract exact strings and ratio from source code..
(NOTE : it did work for me and i try to make it generic but i am not 100% sure that it will work for you also)

Run that script in console:

{
const html = document.querySelectorAll('pre, code, textarea')[0].textContent;
const data = JSON.parse(html.match(/"data":\[([\d.,\s]+)\]/)[0].replace('"data":', ''));
const dataMax = Math.max(...data);

let type, u;
if (/"min":([\d.]+)/.test(html)) {
    type = "A";
    const yMin = parseFloat(html.match(/"min":([\d.]+)/)[1]);
    u = Number((dataMax / (dataMax - yMin)).toFixed(1));
} else if (/y2/.test(html)) {
    type = "B";
    u = 1;
} else if (/reverse.*true/.test(html)) {
    type = "C";
    u = 1;
} else if (/logarithmic/.test(html)) {
    type = "D";
    const first = data[1] - data[0];
    const last = data[data.length-1] - data[data.length-2];
    u = Number((last / Math.max(0.1, first)).toFixed(1));
}

function X(t, o) {
    if (t === "A") { let n = o.toFixed(1); return [`inflates tiny deltas by ${n}x`, `magnifies small movement about ${n}x`, `makes mild change look ${n}x`] }
    if (t === "B") return ["rescaled axis fakes synchronized trend", "dual-axis scaling manufactures false correlation", "secondary scale distorts cross-series comparison", `right axis stretched by ${o.toFixed(1)}x`]
    if (t === "C") return ["inverted axis flips decline narrative", "descending scale reverses trend meaning", "axis direction turns fall into rise"]
    return ["log scale compresses linear acceleration", "log axis hides arithmetic growth pace", "linear growth appears flattened on log", `growth visually compressed by ${o.toFixed(1)}x`]
}

console.log("Type:", type);
console.log("o =", u);
console.log("Valid phrases:", X(type, u));
}

title: TDS Analytics: course performance data across 4 terms
content:
Built a dashboard visualizing TDS assignment data across terms 2025-01 through 2026-01.

What it covers:

  • Score distributions and completion rates per assignment
  • Question-level heatmaps showing which questions most students scored on
  • Submission timing patterns
  • Student retention across assignments
  • Cross-term difficulty trends

Link: TDS Analytics — Tools in Data Science

A few things worth knowing:

Numbers are computed from raw submission data so there may be very minor differences from official records in some edge cases, nothing significant.

Jan 2026 GA1 submissions were too large to process fully, so that assignment is missing the question heatmap and some deeper analysis. Everything else for that term is intact.

No individual student data is stored or shown, all figures are cohort-level aggregates.

Happy to hear if something looks off or doesn’t match what you’d expect.

GA-1 submissions could be compressed to capture top 100 unique submission patterns, to save memory, i did that a while back, in total it was around 38 mb after compression

“https://tds-subs.netlify.app/” do u wanna fork this.. to update your site ? Maybe you can create a cron job in github, to auto sync from the exam site’s submission endpoint…as the course progresses.You could create a pretty good portal to track all this submission data, can try using upstash for db, works well in free tier.

Out of curiosity.. How did you get the data of all the submissions?

While exploring the TDS exam portal I noticed a /filter endpoint that exposes submission data so i wrote a script to fetch it across all assignments and terms, then aggregated everything into the stats you see here.

Surprised to see average completion rate being similar to last term even though particularly this term was harder considering roe

It will be interesting to see that how students of t2 2026 will gonna perform in tds cuz the new content which they added seems pretty interesting and pretty hard compared to our term

title: Announcement Jan 2026 : Bonus Activity assignment

TDS Bonus Activity: Learning Trace Research

We are conducting a study to evaluate the effectiveness of the “no-content” pedagogical model used this term. Since you are solving assignments primarily through independent research and LLMs, we want to understand the specific cognitive paths you take to reach your solutions.
